title: Turning Toward
logline: At a three-wheeler stand a driver's eyes move to every passer-by, and in a fraction of a second, before anyone speaks, he has already settled it: customer, or not.

object.note: Object 5 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The instant before naming carries into a town's three-wheeler stand, where a driver's eyes turn to each passer-by and a judgement forms before anyone speaks.

thread_out.thread: From faces glimpsed and let go to a place long remembered: a woman returning after years of work abroad, the other side of the choice left open in 'Not Yet Decided'.

requirements: A busy three-wheeler stand with drivers willing to be filmed over a working day
A vantage point that can follow both the driver and the passing street
Consent that respects the driver's livelihood and does not slow his actual work

suggestions.name: A busy stand in a market town
suggestions.region: Any market town, to be selected
suggestions.why: Three-wheeler stands are a near-universal feature of Sri Lankan town life; a specific town is left open.
suggestions.verify: A specific stand and a willing driver are unconfirmed.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Before we know anything about what caught our eye, the mind has already turned toward it, and that turning cannot recognise anything; it only points. Settling what the thing is comes a moment later, and still before any response.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: යමක් ඇසට හසු වූ විට එය කුමක්දැයි දැනගන්නට පෙරම සිත ඒ දෙසට හැරෙන අතර, එය කුමක්දැයි නිශ්චය වන්නේ මොහොතකට පසුව, තවමත් ප්‍රතිචාරයකට පෙරය.
lesson.the_teaching: The texts describe 'adverting' (āvajjana), a functional mind that turns the mind-stream toward a new sight or sound; it has no power to know the object, which is known by the seeing that follows it (C010). After receiving and investigating, the same kind of mind does the job of 'determining' (voṭṭhapana), fixing that 'this object is such', and like adverting it is neither wholesome nor unwholesome (C010). The Abhidhamma lists these as separate functions in a relay, and even a mind that can do several jobs does only one at a time (C034). Effort itself is absent from the bare sensing and receiving moments and appears only in some others (C025).
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Through a long day at the stand the camera watches the driver's eyes move across the street: hundreds of small turnings, most leading nowhere, a few becoming a call or a fare. The repeated rhythm of glance, sizing-up, and call or silence lets the viewer notice the turn that comes before any judgement is made.

key_terms.en: adverting: turning the mind-stream toward an object
determining: fixing what the object is, just before impulsion
function or job a mind-moment performs

lesson.caution: Turning toward is not 'mindfulness' or 'being present': the texts say it happens in everyone automatically, with no quality of care or awareness attached.
lesson.builds_on: The flower market showed bare colour arriving before any name; this film steps back one beat further, to the mind turning toward something before it has even been seen.
